extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for NIH R01 grants and NIH peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: The standard NIH review framework used to score R01 research project grant applications (pre-Jan 2025), centering on the five scored criteria (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) plus overall impact and scoring rules. Intended to guide reviewers' evaluations and inform applicants about what reviewers consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The application should challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions. Concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions should be novel to one field of research or novel in a broad sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The program director(s)/principal investigator(s) (PDs/PIs), collaborators, and other researchers should be well suited to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If early-stage investigators or those in the early stages of independent careers, they should have appropriate experience and training. If established, they should have demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Are the concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions novel to one field of research or novel in a broad sense?

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the Specific Aims of the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have the investigators included plans to address weaknesses in the rigor of prior research? Have the investigators presented strategies to ensure a robust and unbiased approach? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented? If the project is in the early stages of development, will the strategy establish feasibility?

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate whether the institutional resources are appropriate to ensure the successful execution of the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact Scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall impact score reflects reviewers' judgment of the extent to which the project can make an impact. NIH defines impact as the likelihood that your project will exert a powerful influence on its field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact score is NOT a mathematical sum or mean of the criterion scores. Reviewers are instructed to weigh the different criteria as they see fit in deriving their overall scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assign a criterion score from 1 to 9 (where 1 is best) to each core NIH review criterion. The score scale is 1 (exceptional) to 9 (poor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final overall impact score is the average of all eligible reviewer scores multiplied by 10 (e.g., a 2.7 average becomes a 27).
